summary:
Astrosence– Astronaut Health Monitoring System

Astrosence is a health-monitoring application designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It integrates essential health indicators, such as heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, and body temperature, with daily health records to provide a more comprehensive view of an astronaut’s health status. The application evaluates changes in these indicators, highlights potential health risks, and provides alerts when predefined warning or critical thresholds are reached.

Astrosence also includes a What-If Predictive Simulation feature, allowing astronauts to explore how planned activities or changes in their daily schedules may affect their health-management indicators. Additionally, its daily tracking system combines manually entered information, such as sleep, hydration, exercise, and radiation exposure, with available health measurements to monitor trends over time.

By bringing health monitoring, risk assessment, predictive planning, and daily tracking into one platform, Astrosence aims to help astronauts recognize potential concerns earlier and make more informed decisions throughout their missions.
details:
AstroSence is a health-monitoring application that we developed to help astronauts keep track of their health during long space missions. We wanted to create one platform that brings together important health information and helps astronauts understand changes in their health.

The application has three main sections. The first is the Health Monitoring Dashboard, where astronauts can view important measurements such as heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation (SpO₂), respiratory rate, and body temperature. The app compares these readings with predefined thresholds, highlights unusual values, and sends alerts when a reading reaches a warning or critical level. It also calculates a Monitoring Priority Index to show which health indicators need more attention.

The second section is the What-If Simulation, which allows astronauts to explore how planned activities and changes in their daily schedules may affect their health-management indicators. The third section is Daily Health Tracking, where astronauts can record information such as sleep, exercise, water intake, radiation exposure, and bone health. This helps them follow their records and notice changes over time.

We built AstroSence using Python and Streamlit, with HTML and CSS for the interface and SQLite for storing records. We also used Visual Studio Code for development and GitHub for managing the code. AI tools, including ChatGPT, helped us during development by explaining coding concepts, suggesting ways to organize the application, assisting with writing and debugging Python code, and improving the wording of our project descriptions. Our team reviewed and adapted these suggestions while building the application.

What makes our project different is that it combines health monitoring, alerts, daily tracking, and What-If simulations in one application. We focused on making it easy to use while considering the challenges of living and working in space. Our goal is to help astronauts recognize possible health concerns earlier and make better-informed decisions during their missions.

The current prototype uses simulated demonstration data and manually entered measurements. Direct connections to medical sensors and live NASA datasets are possible future developments.
